output:
**No, this pipeline isn't safe for that.** One renamed parameter in an agent's pull request can delete the customer orders database or the uploads storage account. Nothing in the pipeline would catch it, and the reviewer wouldn't see it in the diff.

**What I found**
- **The deploy deletes anything missing from the template.** `.github/workflows/deploy.yml:40` runs `--mode Complete`, which deletes every resource in `app-prod` that `infra/main.bicep` doesn't declare. If an agent renames `storageName` (`main.bicep:3`) or the `'orders'` database name (`main.bicep:11`), the deploy creates a new empty resource and deletes the old one. If it drops a resource block, that resource is deleted too.
- **Nothing previews the real effect.** The pull request job only builds and lints the template (`deploy.yml:21-22`). Nothing runs `what-if`, a preview of what the deploy would change, either at review time or just before the deploy.
- **The data has no deletion protection.** The database and storage account have no delete locks. The deploy identity holds Owner on the whole subscription, so it could remove any lock anyway, and any mistake reaches beyond `app-prod`.
- **The required human review reads the text, not the effect.** On a large agent pull request, a deletion caused by Complete mode doesn't show up as a removed line. One approval doesn't cover that.

The decision is to stop merging infrastructure pull requests until this is fixed (the record calls this **Block**).

**Why it matters**
Deleting the database or the storage account loses customer data. Running the deploy again won't bring it back. Whether a backup could is not checked. Today it takes one merged pull request. If nothing changes, the risk grows with every large agent pull request, because those are the hardest to review by eye.

**Do this first**
1. In `.github/workflows/deploy.yml:40`, remove `--mode Complete`. The default mode doesn't delete resources missing from the template. Opt into Complete mode only for a specific change, never as the default.
2. Run `az deployment group what-if -g app-prod -f infra/main.bicep --no-pretty-print` in both jobs: in the pull request job (after `azure/login`), with the result posted for the reviewer, and in the deploy job right before `create`. Fail the job when the output shows a `Delete` of a data-holding resource, or a new data-holding resource that replaces an existing one. The only exception is a resource listed by ID in a release file in the same pull request.
3. Add `CanNotDelete` locks to the database and storage account. Replace the subscription Owner role with a role scoped to `app-prod` that can't delete locks, for example Contributor on that resource group.

**What I did not check**
I couldn't check any live settings: this folder isn't a git repository, and I made no calls to GitHub or Azure.
- Branch protection and CODEOWNERS. The `pull_request` trigger only watches `infra/**`, so a pull request that edits `deploy.yml` itself skips validation. Check with `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/branches/main/protection`.
- Reviewers and branch rules on the `production` environment: `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/environments/production`.
- What the federated login credential is restricted to (which repo, branch or environment): `az ad app federated-credential list --id $AZURE_CLIENT_ID`.
- The deploy identity's actual role assignments: `az role assignment list --assignee $AZURE_CLIENT_ID --all`.
- What the current template would delete right now. Resources created by hand in the group are at risk, and Complete mode may also delete the SQL server referenced as `existing` (`main.bicep:5`). Check with `az resource list -g app-prod` and `az deployment group what-if -g app-prod -f infra/main.bicep --mode Complete`.
- Existing locks: `az lock list -g app-prod`.
- Backup retention for the database and storage: `az sql db ltr-policy show`, and `az storage account blob-service-properties show` to see soft-delete and point-in-time restore. The Key Vault template (`main.bicep:23`) doesn't turn on purge protection.

```
Scope:          .github/workflows/deploy.yml → az deployment group create, RG app-prod, environment production
Decision:       Block
Risk:           destructive-change, IaC, preflight, secret (over-privileged identity), concurrency, health-check, rollout
Artifact:       infra/main.bicep from checkout at push SHA; no compiled artifact, digest, or retention
Release state:  BLOCKED
Test evidence:  PR: bicep build + lint only. No IaC security scan, no what-if, no policy check.
Preflight:      None. No what-if before mutation; no destructive-change gate; no lock check.
Strategy:       production-only, no progressive exposure (infra deploy straight to prod)
Representativeness: n/a (no verification stage exists)
Rollout:        in-place, --mode Complete; no exposure switch; no re-promotable known-good template
Zero-downtime:  no. A rename replaces data-holding resources and Complete mode deletes the originals.
Rollback:       none; deleted SQL DB / storage account are not restored by redeploy
Owner handoff:  missing
Evidence:       deploy.yml:16-22 (validate has no login/what-if), :40 (--mode Complete), :10-12 (id-token at workflow level, also granted to PR job); main.bicep:2-3,11 (resource names are parameters/literals, a rename means replacement), :9-21 (no locks); user statement: deploy identity = subscription Owner; 1 human approval
Verification:   Not run. No access to GitHub repo settings or the Azure subscription from this workspace.
Next action:    Remove --mode Complete; add what-if destructive-change gate in PR and in the deploy job before create; CanNotDelete locks on orders DB and uploads storage; scope the identity to app-prod without Microsoft.Authorization/locks/delete; add concurrency: { group: deploy-prod, cancel-in-progress: false }
```
